title: Audit trail for break changes: who, when, before/after, ticket id
subtitle: Insert-only table, 7-year retain, no PAN/SSN. Application logs for 30 days are not a control. Helen Cho is the export consumer.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Helen Cho (Clearhaven ops / internal audit liaison), Priya Nair (EM), Sneha Iyer (QA). Copy Rahul Deshmukh and Kavya Menon.
owners: Aman Kumar (requirements and break-svc), Helen Cho (control owner, export acceptance), Priya Nair (scope freeze)
related: CLH-TDD-2022-021, CH-BRK-104, CH-BRK-118, CH-SEC-044, CH-OPS-0881, NS-CTRL-CLH-AT-01
summary: Requirements for an immutable audit trail of changes to break records on Clearhaven recon. Every change to a break (status, assignee, match key, suppress flag, comment) must record who, when, before, after, and the ticket id. Retain 7 years. Store in an insert-only Postgres table break.audit_event; no UPDATE, no DELETE from application roles. Helen Cho exports for Clearhaven internal audit. Do not write full PAN or SSN. There should not be any on these records; CUSIP is allowed. Rejected: keeping application logs 30 days and calling that the control. This document is the control language plus the schema an engineer can build against.
form_description: Requirements for Clearhaven break-change audit trail: insert-only 7-year store, Helen Cho's export, prohibition on PAN/SSN, and rejection of 30-day application logs as the control.
revision_history: Draft after Helen's Oct 28 request. Schema sketch with Kavya.
Helen marked 30-day logs as non-compliant. Added control language section.
Sneha test cases. Priya froze scope: break changes only, not Kafka payloads.
Approved. Ticket CH-BRK-104. Export format frozen as CSV + SHA-256 manifest.

blocks.text: Control statement (skim this)

blocks.label: Control NS-CTRL-CLH-AT-01
blocks.text: Clearhaven recon shall record every operator or system change to a break in an insert-only store, with actor, timestamp (ET stored as timestamptz UTC), before-image, after-image, and originating ticket id. Records shall be retained 7 years from event_at. Application roles shall not UPDATE or DELETE audit rows. Exports for internal audit shall be produced by Helen Cho's role without engineering hand-edits. Full PAN and SSN shall not be written. CUSIP, ISIN, and internal account_ref may be written. Application logs with a 30-day retention are not this control and shall not be cited as this control.

That paragraph is what Helen will paste into the 2022 year-end control pack. The rest of this document is how we actually do it in break-svc and Postgres clh-recon-prod (today still the 2021 RDS instance, name will change when the recon platform design lands; the requirement follows the data, not the hostname).
Why this exists

On October 12, 2022, Clearhaven internal audit (Helen coordinating, not a named external firm) asked who changed break BRK-88421 from OPEN to SUPPRESSED on September 29 and under which ticket. We had Datadog logs for ingest-api and break-svc with 30-day retention. September 29 was 13 days outside the window. The operator who clicked Suppress was gone from the Slack channel. match-engine does not log the UI actor; it logs the service account break-svc-prod. Ticket CH-OPS-0881 existed but was not stored on the row. Helen spent 6.4 hours reconstructing from email. She then asked for a real audit trail. This is that ask, written so Priya can schedule it and Sneha can test it.

Scope is break changes. A break is a row in break.exception_queue plus the related break.leg_status rows that ops mutates from the break UI and from the bulk CSV Helen's team still drops on SFTP. Out of scope for this document: Kafka payload archival, AMI ssh sessions, RDS admin queries, and match-engine's internal matchkey cache. Rahul asked to include 'everything.' Priya froze to breaks. If audit wants match decisions later, that is a different REQ.
Rejected: 30-day application logs as the control

blocks.label: Rejected alternative
blocks.text: CH-BRK-104 comment 3 (Rahul Deshmukh, November 4): extend Datadog log retention to 90 days, add actor_id to the JSON log line, call it done. Helen rejected it November 7 in writing. I am rejecting it here so it does not reappear as a sprint compromise.
Why logs fail as this control, in the language Helen needs and in the language we need.

Retention. Datadog index clh-prod-apps is 30 days. Security's S3 archive of the same logs is 365 days, not 7 years, and it is not queryable by ops. Turning the index to 7 years is a cost Diego quoted at $18.4k/mo extra at today's ingest volume (12.6 GB/day of app logs, most of it Kafka consumer chatter). We would be paying to keep match-engine partition assignment logs so that once a quarter Helen can find a Suppress click. That is the wrong store.

Integrity. Log lines are not insert-only in the sense a table with REVOKE UPDATE is. Shippers drop. We sampled October: 0.18% of break-svc lines missing versus stdout on the host, traced to the Datadog agent restart on me-worker-05b (yes, the snowflake). An auditor who asks 'show me every change to BRK-88421' cannot be told 'except when the agent bounced.' The table has to live next to the break row, in the same transaction, or we do not claim completeness.

Actor. Today's log line is actor=svc-break. The UI authenticates against Clearhaven Okta, then break-svc uses a service account to write Postgres. Unless we pass the Okta subject into the write path and persist it, extending log retention just stores a more durable lie. The requirement is the human or the job name, not the JDBC user.

Ticket id. Logs do not have it unless the operator typed it into a comment field. Half the time they do not. The control says ticket id is required on every mutating call. That is an API change, not a log-shipping change.
Export. Helen cannot run a Datadog query in 2029. She can run a SQL export or a CSV job we give her. Logs fail that test even if we kept them.
So: not Datadog, not CloudWatch, not 'we grep the host.' Table. Insert-only. 7 years. Build it once.
In scope / out of scope

blocks.text: Required fields

Every audit row. No optional-in-practice fields. If the API cannot fill ticket_id, it must reject the mutation with 400 and not write the break change. That will annoy ops for a week. Helen said that is acceptable. Rahul said it would slow month-end. Priya said ticket_id can be the Jira key or the ops ticket or the string 'MONTH-END-YYYY-MM' for the standing close procedure, not a blank.

blocks.caption: break.audit_event columns. Types are Postgres. Names are frozen so Sneha can write tests against them.
rows: Stable id for export and for the hash chain.
Clock from the database (clock_timestamp()), not the app server. Store UTC. Display ET in the export.
human = Okta subject. job = batch. system = constraint trigger inside Postgres (rare).
Okta email or subject, or job name like job:break-csv-apply. Max 254 chars.
Jira CH-* or ops ticket or MONTH-END-YYYY-MM. Max 64. No empty string.
BRK-... business id, not only the bigserial, because the bigserial is not what Helen searches.
Null if the change is queue-level only.
status_change, assignee_change, comment_add, suppress_set, matchkey_override, create, bulk_apply.
Subset of fields that changed, plus the fields needed to identify the row. Not the whole exception_queue tuple.
Same shape as before_image. create has after only.
From the UI request. Null for jobs. Do not fail the write if missing.
break-svc tag, e.g. 2.1.4. So we know which code wrote the row.
SHA-256 of canonical JSON of the other columns except row_hash. Detect silent edits.

blocks.text: before_image and after_image are field subsets, not dumps of PII-heavy legs. Allowed keys: status, assignee, suppress_flag, suppress_reason, comment, match_key, account_ref, cusip, isin, qty, settle_date, contra, ticket_id_on_break (if we store one there). Disallowed keys: pan, ssn, tax_id, account_number_full, anything named like card+. If a developer adds a key, the write path must strip it. Sneha tests that. See Sensitive fields.
Immutability

Application roles break_app, break_readonly, and helen_audit shall have INSERT (break_app only) and SELECT. No UPDATE. No DELETE. No TRUNCATE. Enforce in Postgres, not in Java. Java will have a bug eventually. The GRANT is the control.

blocks.caption: Skeleton. Exact SQL will live in the migrate next to this REQ. Do not run this against prod from a laptop; Kavya applies via the migrate path.

blocks.text: Triggers. A BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that RAISE EXCEPTION 'audit_event is insert-only' is belt-and-suspenders for the migrate role, which has to own the table and therefore could UPDATE. The migrate role should not be used by break-svc. Sneha: test that break_app UPDATE returns an error, not a silent 0 rows. Test that a superuser can still UPDATE (disaster recovery) and that we log that in pgaudit. Superuser edits are a Sev-2 conversation with Helen, not a feature.

Same transaction as the break write. break-svc must INSERT audit_event in the same Postgres transaction as the UPDATE to exception_queue. If the audit INSERT fails (ticket_id missing, redaction function exception), the break change rolls back. Ops will see an error in the UI. That is the point. Do not queue the audit write to Kafka 'to keep the UI fast.' We timed the extra INSERT at 2.4-4.1 ms on a staging copy of 1.8M breaks. Month-end bulk CSV of 12,400 rows would add ~40s if serial; batch the audit inserts in the same transaction as the bulk apply, not one round trip each, but still the same transaction. If the transaction is too large, chunk by 500 breaks, each chunk its own transaction with its own audit rows. Do not apply 500 and then audit 0.
Retention: 7 years
event_at + 7 years. Not '7 years from break close.' A break can reopen. The audit row's clock is the change, not the break lifecycle. Helen confirmed November 10.

We will not delete at 7 years + 1 day automatically in v1. v1 is keep everything we have, which will not be 7 years of data until 2029. A purge job is a 2028 problem. Documenting a purge now so nobody 'helps' by adding a cron. When we purge, it will be a dated job, Helen-approved, with an export of the to-be-deleted slice stored in s3://clh-audit-export-prod/retention-purge/YYYY/ with the same CSV+hash format. Until then, no DELETE, including 'cleanup of test rows' in prod. Staging can TRUNCATE. Prod cannot.

Volume guess, so Diego can size disks. Today Helen's team mutates ~4,200 breaks per business day (April-October 2022 average 4,184; month-end days 11,200-14,600). At ~800 bytes per audit row plus jsonb, call it 1.2 KB. 4,200 * 1.2 KB * 252 business days ~ 1.27 GB/year. 7 years ~ 8.9 GB plus indexes, call it 14 GB. RDS clh-recon-prod has 400 GB allocated, 142 GB used. This table is not a capacity event. Partitioning by month can wait until we are past 50 GB or until the recon platform design (CLH-TDD-2022-021) anyway. Do not block v1 on partitions.
Sensitive fields: no full PAN/SSN

Break records should not contain PAN or SSN today. I grepped a staging snapshot (November 8, 2.1M exception_queue rows, 6.4M leg_status rows) for 9-digit tokens and Luhn-passing 16-digit tokens in comment and in raw_ref. Hits: 14 comments with what look like SSNs typed by ops ('ssn last4 4412' is fine; 'ssn 219-00-4412' appeared 3 times; 11 other 9-digit strings that might be internal ids). Zero Luhn-passing PANs. Those 3 comments are enough to write a redaction rule. We do not assume the grep is complete.

items: Do not persist PAN (15-19 digit card-like, Luhn pass) in before_image, after_image, or comment. Replace with [PAN-REDACTED].
Do not persist SSN (xxx-xx-xxxx or 9 digits adjacent to the tokens ssn, social, tin). Replace with [SSN-REDACTED]. Last4 alone may stay if not adjacent to those tokens.
CUSIP (9 character alphanumeric) is allowed. ISIN is allowed. account_ref (Clearhaven internal, e.g. CH-ACC-10442) is allowed. qty and settle_date are allowed.
If the redaction function throws, the transaction fails. Do not skip redaction on error.
Do not log the pre-redaction comment to Datadog either. That would recreate the 30-day problem with worse data. Redact before any logger sees it.

blocks.text: CUSIP is the identifier ops uses to talk to Marcus and to counterparties. If we strip CUSIP, the export is useless. Helen was explicit. Security (Jordan Hale, CH-SEC-044) agreed CUSIP is not PAN. Do not 'just in case' hash CUSIPs. I have seen that idea in two Slack threads this month. It dies here.
Export for Helen

Helen is the control owner and the person who will sit with internal audit. Engineering does not hand-build CSVs the night before. v1 export is a SQL view plus a job she can run, or that Aman runs with her on the call for the first two cycles, then she runs.

blocks.caption: Export contract. Change this only with Helen's initials.
rows: CSV, UTF-8, header row, comma, quotes if needed. Plus a SHA-256 of the CSV bytes in a sidecar .sha256 file.
audit_id, event_at_et, actor_type, actor_id, ticket_id, break_id, leg_id, action, before_image, after_image, src_ip, app_version, row_hash_hex
event_at_et is America/New_York, format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. row still stored UTC.
required: event_at range. optional: break_id, actor_id, ticket_id, action.
s3://clh-audit-export-prod/helen/YYYY/MM/dd-HHmmssZ.csv and .sha256. Bucket is write for the job role, read for Helen's IAM. No public ACL.
CSV with header only, still hashed. Do not skip the file. Absence is not 'no events.'
role helen_audit SELECT on break.audit_event and on view break.v_audit_event_et. No INSERT. No RDS console.
on request, plus a standing first-Monday-after-month-end export of the prior month. First standing run: January 3, 2023 if v1 is live.

blocks.text: Rejected: emailing the CSV to Helen. Mailboxes are not a 7-year store and they forward. S3 plus her IAM. Marcus asked if the TAM should get a copy. No. Internal audit only. If a regulator asks, Helen pulls, she does not CC the TAM by default.

The view break.v_audit_event_et is a convenience for timezone. It must not hide columns. It must not join to exception_queue in a way that would drop audit rows whose break was later deleted (breaks should not be deleted either; if they are, the audit row still exports). LEFT JOIN if you join at all. v1 can skip the join and export audit_event only. Helen said she will join in Excel if she has to. Fine.
API and UI requirements

break-svc mutating endpoints (PATCH /breaks/{id}, POST /breaks/{id}/comments, POST /breaks/bulk) require header X-Ticket-Id or a JSON field ticket_id. Missing: 400, no write. The UI gets a required ticket field. Bulk CSV requires a column ticket_id or a filename pattern CH-NNNNN.csv. Filename pattern is already how Helen drops files (CH-OPS-*.csv). Keep it. If both filename and column exist and disagree, 400 the file, do not pick one.

Actor. UI sends the Okta access token. break-svc validates, writes actor_id from the token subject/email, actor_type=human. Jobs use a mapped identity from the Kubernetes service account or the EC2 instance profile name today (we are still on EC2 workers; do not write i-0... as actor_id, write job:break-csv-apply). System triggers inside Postgres, if any, write actor_type=system and actor_id=trigger:break_status_guard. We do not plan a trigger in v1 that mutates breaks; this is so the check constraint has somewhere to go.

Read path for ops. GET /breaks/{id}/audit returns the rows for that break_id, newest first, page size 50. This is not the 7-year export. It is so the next Helen can see who suppressed BRK-88421 without a SQL client. Same redaction. Same columns. Sneha tests that a user without break.read.audit does not get the route (403). Role mapping is Okta group clh-ops-audit vs clh-ops. clh-ops can mutate (today). clh-ops-audit can read audit. Helen is in both. Junior ops is in clh-ops only until Helen says otherwise. That last sentence is Helen's, November 10.

blocks.text: Failure modes
Ops types ticket_id=n/a to get past the UI

We will see it. Constraint is length >= 1, not 'looks like CH-'. I will not build a regex that guesses Jira. Helen can query actor+ticket_id='n/a' in the first month and train people. If after 60 days it is still common, we add a check against a small allowlist of patterns. Not v1. Do not reject MONTH-END-2022-11; that is a valid standing ticket per Priya.
Clock skew on app servers

We use clock_timestamp() in Postgres, so AMI drift on the workers (real, see the openssl and chrony mess) does not stamp audit rows. Good. The UI will still display local times. Export uses ET from the timestamptz. If RDS clock is wrong we have a bigger problem; Diego owns NTP on RDS. Out of scope except to say: do not use the JVM clock for event_at.
Someone grants UPDATE to break_app during an incident

They will, to 'fix a bad row.' Trigger plus missing RLS policy should still block. If a superuser updates, pgaudit must catch it and page Helen. Diego: confirm pgaudit is on for this table when the migrate lands. If pgaudit cannot filter per table, page on any superuser UPDATE in schema break. Noisy. Correct.
jsonb before/after misses a field ops actually changed

Then the control is incomplete. v1 allowlist of keys is in Required fields. Adding a new mutable column on exception_queue without adding it to the allowlist is a failed story, not a nice-to-have. PR template for break-svc should ask 'does this mutate a break field? if yes, audit key listed?' Sneha can fail the story. Kavya, put it on the template.
What we are not building in v1

items: Hash chain across rows (row_hash is per-row, not chained to previous audit_id). Chaining is a 2023 maybe. Per-row hash still detects in-place edits.
UI pretty-diff. Export and GET JSON are enough. Rahul wanted a red/green diff. Not v1.
Shipping audit_event to Kafka. The table is the store. A CDC topic can come later for the warehouse; it is not the control.
Using application logs, 30 days or otherwise, as a substitute.

blocks.text: Engineer build notes

Implement in break-svc, repo ns-clh-break, package com.northstar.clearhaven.breaksvc.audit. Do not implement in match-engine. Match-engine should not UPDATE exception_queue status except through a break-svc call, and today it still does for auto-MATCHED. That auto-MATCHED path is in scope (action=status_change, actor_type=job, actor_id=job:match-engine). Kavya: that is a one-day change in match-engine to call break-svc or to INSERT audit_event itself with the same schema. Prefer call break-svc so the allowlist and redaction live in one place. If latency is a problem (match-engine is on the EC2 workers, break-svc is four other boxes, RTT 1.2-3.8 ms in-AZ), a direct INSERT from match-engine with a shared library is acceptable. Two copies of redaction are not. Shared library, one jar, same version.

Migrate version: next after current flyway on clh-recon-prod, which is V12 as of November 16. This will be V13. Do not bundle unrelated schema in V13. If recon platform design wants to rename schemas, it can move audit_event later; the requirement is the table behavior, not the name break.audit_event forever. Export column names stay even if the table moves; the view can alias.

items: V13: CREATE TABLE, indexes, GRANTs, RLS, trigger, view v_audit_event_et. No backfill. We do not invent history we do not have. Helen knows October 12 cannot be reconstructed. Say that in the control pack.
break-svc: ticket_id required, redaction, same-transaction INSERT, GET /audit, 403 by role.

match-engine auto-MATCHED: call or shared INSERT, actor job:match-engine, ticket_id=SYSTEM-MATCH until Helen gives a better standing id. Open question if she hates SYSTEM-MATCH; default it anyway so we do not block matching.
CSV bulk: filename/column ticket rules, chunked transactions.
Export job: Airflow or a CronJob, S3 prefix above, Helen IAM. Aman runs with her in December if code is late.
Sneha: AT-01 through AT-14 on staging with a copy of prod-like grants (staging today has everyone as superuser; that would fake AT-03. Fix staging grants first or the tests are theater).

blocks.text: Ask of Helen and Priya

Helen: this control language and the export contract are yours to accept. If internal audit wants a vendor name on the store, there is not one. It is Postgres you already run. If they want 10 years, say so before V13; 7 is what you wrote on October 28. If they want PAN hashed rather than absent, that is a different document and I will push back, because we should not have PAN at all.

Priya: freeze holds. v1 is the table, the API, the export, the tests. Not Kafka archive, not UI diff, not 7-year purge. CH-BRK-104 is the epic. I want it in the December 12 release if Kavya's match-engine call is in by December 5. If not, January 9, still before Helen's January 3 standing export... which would then slip to February 6. Call that in planning. Do not ship a log-based 'temporary control' to hit January 3. That is the rejected alternative with a date on it.
